utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in the courtroom and those supporting us just outside the courtroom. Ms. Mahindaratne, are you ready to resume the examination of the witness Arifagic?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, first of all, we call the case, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You are perfectly right, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Madam Registrar, good morning to you as well. May I ask you to call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Before the case was called, I asked whether the Prosecution was ready to resume the examination of the witness Arifagic and I asked the usher to bring the witness in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Ms. Arifagic, may I still remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration that you gave at the beginning of your testimony. Yes, Ms. Mahindaratne, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Ms. Arifagic, you remember you were examining a document when court adjourned yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May the witness be shown P3738L again, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: You were examining the medical report of Izet Colakovic.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document as an official medical report issued by the hospital and do you recognise the official stamp and your signature on this document?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can you please give the date of admission and the date of injury of the patient.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 12th of July 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I am sorry, Mr. President, there was no translation of the date.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Could you give the date again, please.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 12th of July 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, Mr. President. I was on the wrong channel. May the witness be shown Exhibit number P3738N, translation P3738N1.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document as an official medical report issued by the hospital and do you recognise the official stamp of the hospital and your signature on the document?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Could you give the name of the patient, which is recorded on the document?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sevda Hasanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And could you give the date of admission?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 4th of February 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May the witness be shown Exhibit number P3738O.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document as an official medical report issued by the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you recognise your signature and the official stamp of the hospital on the document?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can you please state the name of the patient and the date of admission.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rajko Maksimovic, 4th of February 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May the witness be shown Exhibit number P3738P, translation, P3738P1.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document as an official report, discharge sheet, issued by the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you recognise your signature and the official stamp of the hospital on the document?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can you please state the name of the patient and the date of admission.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sanela Muratovic, 26th of June 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Could you read out the first line in the box which says, "case history"?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Admitted as an emergency case, wounded by a sniper's bullet."

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May the witness be shown Exhibit number P3738R.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document as an official death certificate issued by the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you recognise your signature and the official seal of the hospital on the document?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My signature is here, but I cannot see the seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well. Can you please state the name of the patient which is recorded on the document?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Asim Zagorica.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And the date of admission?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1st of June 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: In the absence of the official seal, when you cannot see the seal clearly on the document, how could you be certain this is the document -- official document, issued by the hospital? Do you recognise the format of the document?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And, therefore, can you say that this is an official death certificate issued by the hospital by examining the document?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May the witness be shown Exhibit number P3738S.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document as an official death certificate issued by the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you recognise your signature and the official stamp of the hospital on the document?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My signature is here, but I cannot see the seal of the hospital. I don't think that we had the seal at the time that it had been made, because it is only then that the hospital was officially registered at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can you recognise the format of the document being an official form used by the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can you please state the name of the deceased and the date of death.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Atif Bajraktarevic, 1st of June 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May the witness be shown Exhibit number P3369A.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document as an official discharge sheet issued by the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you recognise the official seal of the hospital on the document?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Have you signed this document at any stage or seen this before?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you recognise your signature on the document?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can you please state the name of the patient and the date of admission.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fatima Salcin, 13th of June 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May the witness be shown Exhibit number P3747, translation, P3747.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have a problem here which is that if you have the same copies as we do, most of them are just illegible they are just black boxes, and the rest is not so legible. So I don't know what to do. I asked for other copies. We were told that's all that was. I don't think that the Defence can work usefully with the names that we can't even decipher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is for certain that those parts we cannot read cannot be used, but let's first see what the Prosecution wants to draw our attention to and let's see whether this is in part of the document which is legible, and let's also see whether there is any explanation for this condition of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. In fact, my colleague, Mr. Stamp, responded to the same issue yesterday with regard to the same document. We can only do as best as we could and even the original document that we have, which we have brought down from the ward, is in the same state. And we cannot clean it up beyond that. So this is the reason for the state it is in. And as far as the document is concerned, the Prosecution merely intends to tender it as a list. We do not intend to go into details of the entries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but, of course, if you have a list if you say we want to just establish that there exists a list, I hardly can imagine that the Prosecution would not at least wants to prove as well, what is approximately on that list. So lists without being whatever attention to the content is may not be that useful. I mean, it could be a shopping list of someone. It is not just a list, I take it. So would you please pay attention to that while examining the witness, and if there are any remaining questions we will put them. What else we would like, and what the Chamber would certainly like to know, whether the original of which this was copied is just as badly legible as the original.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I have the original right here that was brought down from the ward.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is the original that comes directly from the ward, so that is the one taken from the ward?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps at a later stage we would like to see then the original. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I have some doubts for the following reasons: The Defence is practically become a specialist in black boxes. We are deciphering them better than anyone else and if we keep each one of these documents, we will see that the dark area at the bottom of the page is always more or less -- has more or less always the same kind of form in the space. It is always the very same dark area on each page, which means that these are not the originals which have dark areas, but it is probably the glass of the photocopier which was possibly clouded or dark. We can see that every time. So, there are clear originals somewhere, certainly, where they come from, and it should be possible, normally speaking, to make copies with a photocopier which is clear and clean. But we can see very well that the problem doesn't come from the originals, but from the copies, and from the means of copying them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, looking at what you call the original, it seems to be a photocopy of the original which might still remain in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: If I may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because I have some difficulties in accepting that this is the original copy that was in Sarajevo. Because the UN stamp, the presiding officer stamp, and the -- that is in blue. So this should be a copy taken from the original which still remains in the Dobrinja hospital or in whatever archive, is that true?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, when I referred to the word "original" I did not mean the original document. Undoubtedly this is a Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. photocopy. But this is the most original document we have here in the OTP. And undoubtedly there is a very clear original document somewhere, but it is not in our premises or it is not within our custody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps you should ask the witness whether the original which is still in Sarajevo would be better legible. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you recognise the document which was just shown to you, P3747?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: The document which has been shown to you is not a clear copy, it is a quite illegible right at the bottom of the document. Are you aware as to where perhaps the original documents may have been or have you seen the original documents at some stage?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is obvious that this is a copy, that this is a poor copy, and the original must exist certainly, considering that Dobrinja hospital was officially closed, all the documents, documentation, have been transferred to the archives of the town and the files of the city, and you can probably find the originals here. But this is certainly the document that belongs to the hospital -- originates from the hospital, I can state it for sure, because most of these people since I worked -- I lived in Dobrinja at the time, I know most people there. And of course, we didn't know at the time that we would be using these documents. We didn't know at the time that we would be here at the Tribunal, but we made them for our own needs.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Were you working at the hospital at the time this document was issued?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Yes, I arrived a short while ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Was it a response to your satisfaction, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, of course, we have to consider, I take it you are going to tender this. Well, the answer is quite clear, but whether that would be sufficient for admitting the document into evidence is a different question, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President. May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can you please state what this document is.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is the list of patients who were brought to the hospital and they were wounded on the 1st of June 1993 at a match in Dobrinja. So this is just a partial list because only part of the patients, because the hospital did not have the capacity to take in all the patients wounded on that day. And this is a very important document indeed, and I would really like you to make an effort and get a hold of the original.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: When you said "wounded", wounded as a result of what?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a result of the shelling.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can you please state the date of admission of the patients, the dates with regard to each patient are the same on the list?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1st of June 1993, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yesterday when you testified with regard to Exhibit number P3738C --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May the witness be shown Exhibit P3738C again, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: You examined this document, compared this document with P3738M, and said that the date on P3738C could be a typographical error, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously I can't state it 100 per cent, but I suppose, since I know that Saida Balicevac and other people on the list are related, were related. So it may be a typing error, but I can't tell with any degree of certainty. Obviously, it says the 4th of May 1994, and there was this massacre on the 4th of February 1994. Since the name of the witness corresponds, I believe that was the date. But I can't say 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Would you be able to answer with any amount of certainty, if you examine the central Registry or the relevant entry in the protocol with regard to that person, would you be certain that this is a typographical error?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if I could find this in the register, a name and the surname, with reference to that date.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, there would be no doubt whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this stage, may I seek permission of the Chamber to show the witness the relevant -- the relevant entries with regard to 4th February 1994 which may assist us to clarify that this is in fact a typographical error. The document has that particular document has already been disclosed to the Defence. It was in fact part of the 92 bis package of Muhamed Musar [phoen] and therefore the Defence has already had the opportunity to examine the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May the witness be shown the relevant entries for 4th February 1994 in the protocol. We have photocopies here if that would assist.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you recognise the document which was just shown to you?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a copy of the patient's register.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Part of it or is it the complete?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a part of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: The dates of the entries or the period to which these -- the excerpts relate to is what?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can you tell what the date of the -- the dates are, at least the period, there are several dates?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In these papers, it is the 4th of February 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Could you examine this document and search for the name which is stated in P3738C, is it indicated in the central Registry?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes it is on page -- on the last page of this set of papers. The number is 761. Said Balicevac, she was born in 1976, the date of birth tallies with the date of birth in the death certificate. So these two dates tally. Their name and surname as well and the date of injury. We have seen -- it must have been a typing error, but the date of birth is the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I see that in the transcript the name has been typed incorrectly. May I just perhaps give it to the -- or to the relevant certificate or the document to the --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can you compare that document P3738C and be certain that it relates to one and the same person.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You mean these two documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, the entry with regard to serial number 761 and document P3738C. Do these relate to one and the same person?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: In the central registry, what is the date of admission?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the central register, the day of admission is the 4th of February 1994, and so the name and surname are the same, the date of birth -- just a moment -- the date of birth, the address, and then on the second page, even though I am not a member of the medical staff myself, but I can see the diagnosis. It is the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, out of these documents, which one is made first what is the initial entry which is made?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The patient's register.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Therefore accordingly can you be certain that the date mentioned in P3738C, as 4th May 1994, is a typographical error?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is the 4th of February 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Witness, now all these documents that you have examined yesterday and today are official documents issued by the Dobrinja hospital?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And as such kept under the law of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That is all, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Ms. Mahindaratne. Ms. Pilipovic, is the Defence ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for the record keeping, I have one hour and 20 minutes approximately noted down for the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Madam. Madam, can you confirm that on the 11th of November 1995, you made a statement to the investigators from the Court?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: At that time in 1995, where were you employed?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1995, I worked at the Dobrinja hospital, as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said yesterday that from May 1993 until June 1996 you worked there?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us when the hospital was set up?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was officially set up on the 12th of May, between the 10th and the 12th -- maybe the 10th of May, 1993, officially. But unofficially, it started operating a year earlier due to the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Madam, you have told us now and yesterday during the examination-in-chief you said that you started working in May 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement you said "I held that post since the 10th of May 1992."

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't suppose so. I couldn't have said that, but perhaps it was my mistake, because I saw in the statement and I just -- it was an oversight, but I did not say I worked there, because I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So this statement claiming that you were there as of the 10th of May 1992 is incorrect?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably it was an oversight on my part when I was signing the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On that day, you handed in certain documents to the Prosecution staff?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what documents did the Prosecution ask you for?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably the ones I gave them. You will admit it is a bit difficult for me to remember. They probably asked for the patients' register and the death certificates, presumably.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you telling us that at that stage you had register and these death certificates at the hospital, the ones we were looking at just now and that these were the documents that you handed in?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you were issuing these death certificates and these documents, did you make your own selection or were you asked to hand them in for the exact dates?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain to us how you issued or handed in the certificate for Fatima Salcin? Were you asked to provide some sort of proof, documentary evidence, that Fatima Salcin was treated at the hospital or was it your choice?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To whom? I mean, obviously they did not ask names and surnames, and it was obviously not my choice. It probably just happened to be with all the other documents. I don't see for what reason that particular patient would be special.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: That is what I am asking you.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't understand. Her name was or her certificates were probably in the files by accident. I really don't know. Why would I have chosen her in particular?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: According to that principle yours handed in the document referring to Sanela Murakovic?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, what principle are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, by accident --

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably nothing was there by accident --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you, you are speaking the same language. Everything has to be translated, so may I ask you to make a short pause after the question so that the interpreters can follow us. Please proceed. Ms. Pilipovic, of course the same is valid for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Madam, is it true that the Prosecution investigators asked for you to display documents referring to specific dates in 1992, 1993 and Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 1994 that is to say, didn't they tell you we need documentation referring to such-and-such a date? And then you provided these documents?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I simply don't understand. I don't remember whether they referred to specific dates or periods of time. I can't remember. But whatever I was asked to do, whatever I was asked to provide, and if the documents were kept in the archives, they could get them and anyone else as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You are saying that everything was in the archives of the hospital. Can you tell us where the archives were situated?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At a premises of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: The register that you say were kept at the hospital, how many did you have?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that particular time, apart from the central part, the hospital had some other offices elsewhere, so we had to move as little as possible so we did have units at quadrant C5 Dobrinja 5, and Dobrinja I, so they had their own registers.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: As to the registers of those offices, were they kept?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ones that were being used were there and the ones that were finished were brought back to the central hospital, and the reports were submitted from those outside surgeries to the central hospital for reasons of evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Have I understand --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please slow down with the questions as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The interpreters request me that you slow down as well. Yes. You really have to take breaks. If you look at the screen, as soon as the cursor stops moving, then at least we have the translation ready. So would you please keep an eye on that as well, Ms. Arifagic. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Madam, could you confirm that the reports from those regional surgeries, as it were, were enclosed to the main register?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us who was in charge of the register?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean, the name and surname? The administrative official who was in charge of the registers, he was at the reception, and whilst medical staff was carrying out their part of the job that administrative official would enter the name of the patient into the register.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Would you record the time of admission in the register?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date, yes, but I am not sure about the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You have looked at the death certificate for the dates of the 1st of June, the 12th of July, and the 4th of February. Can you tell us on the basis of what data you opted for these dates and these death certificates?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't select them, probably, and I know that on those three dates that terrible things had happened, and I think that it is an excellent idea for those dates to be selected. What happened was horrendous and I was there and I witnessed it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I asked you who told you, who gave you these dates?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you do not wish to tell me the truth?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have told you I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Today during the examination-in-chief, you looked at these death certificates. Can you tell us where the time of death is ascertained?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure I have grasped the question. Probably -- well, the patients would be brought to the hospital and if the death occurs at the hospital, it would be at the hospital. Normally, everybody would be brought to the hospital together and then we would separate them.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you are telling us that in the case of death of patients who died at the hospital, the death would be ascertained at the hospital premises?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Who at the hospital would ascertain the death?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The doctor.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When a doctor ascertains the death of a patient at the hospital, what data are entered into the files and where?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am really not a doctor. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, what form is used by such a doctor? Is there a specific form?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you have had the opportunity of seeing it in the documents. There is a special form, the death certificate form, which is then submitted to the municipality, one copy sent to the family, and one is kept at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Have I understood you correctly that these forms, these death certificates that you have looked at, are the death certificates that you kept at the hospital at the time of death and which were filled in and signed by the doctor?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The forms did exist. We drew up these forms because we had no where to buy them at the time. We had all sorts of forms. And in case of need, the doctor who ascertained the death of the patient would fill them in.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When the doctor ascertains a death of a patient, you are telling us that he signs the form and the form is empty prior to filling it out?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that you drew them up yourselves, can you explain to us what technique was used?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't understand the question. The same way you do everything. You have a table, XL, I don't know whether we had that, whether we were so advanced in 1993. We just put a set of tables into the computer and printed it out, that was that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So as far as I can tell, you did have the forms in the computer at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Presumably. Part of it, and I believe there was a printing press at Dobrinja. So some of it was from there and we had photocopies as well. We made due as we best could.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that the forms are the death certificates filled out by doctors, the doctors who ascertained the time of death and they signed the certificates, when you say that you kept those in the computer, are you also telling us that at that time when the death of a patient was ascertained, you had all that in the computer?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, it was the administrative official who had the forms. He had a stack of these forms to make them available to doctors as they were needed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I asked you a question about the death certificates. Today or rather yesterday during the examination-in-chief you looked at the list of patients killed. Let me refer to one date in particular, the 4th of February 1994. It is P3738M.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could the witness be shown that document. P3738M.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, before you, you have a document about which you told us is the document of Dobrinja hospital.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us when was this document compiled?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably one day after this, after what happened. That means the day after the shelling.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So what you are saying is that all of these persons whose names and surnames are here on this list, these are persons who were admitted at the Dobrinja hospital?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were admitted, probably you cannot see it from here, considering the situation that was at the time, the hospital didn't have all the specialists so some cases which could not be treated at Dobrinja hospital they went to the Kosevo Hospital. I don't know whether these cases are those specifically. But I am talking in general.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In this document could you, for instance, look up the name of Sabahudin Ljusa listed under number 3.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Next to what it says "Dobrinja I" does it say 11.15?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us on the basis of what and which data did you enter the time? What does this mean?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Honestly, I didn't enter it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So what you are saying is that you don't know?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the time represents because I didn't enter the data into the computer.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do I understand you correctly that this document was compiled the day after the 4th of February 1994, and that this data was all then entered into the computer?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us which person at the hospital was the one who was working on the computer and entering the data into the computer?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a computer operator. So it wasn't a medical staff. He the person who worked on gathering the data and compiling the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "worked on gathering the data and compiling the report"?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I mean, I am sorry, gathering the data from the area of surgeries, and then he would compile a complete report of the hospital and he was the one who was entering the data.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "worked on entering the data," who was the person who was working on the registration book and who was entering the diagnosis?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The registration book was also done by the person, this lady, who was an administrative assistant. She is not a medical staff. But she was in fact typing out the diagnosis on the orders of the doctors. And she would then enter the diagnosis as told by the doctors.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So what you are saying is that diagnosis was entered into the registration book of the hospital was done by a clerk?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said the diagnosis was inputted in the registration book by the administrative assistant who worked on the orders of a doctor. So not independently. Practically a doctor would be dictating the diagnosis and the administrative assistant would be typing it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: This list for which it says "4th of February 1994" that you see before you was it compared with -- to the registration book of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When I asked you, you said that the registration book of the hospital would not contain the hour, the time?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I wasn't sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: We had the opportunity to see one part of the registration book for the 4th of February 1994 and were able to see that there was no time entered. How do you explain that in this document we do have the time entered?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot explain it. I am not explaining it. I don't know how-- what that time refers to. Perhaps it could be the time that this information, this data, was entered into the computer. I don't know what this time stands for.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, on the basis of which documents did the person who was filling in this document, how could that person enter the diagnosis?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was done on the basis of official reports which were forwarded by the surgeries, that is, the doctors who work in area surgeries, who would then ascertain if this surgery was nearby, if they would ascertain it; or perhaps it would be done at the hospital on the basis of the registration book, which was at the hospital. That is when the report would be compiled. So the report was compiled on the basis of official documents by the people who were in charge for this so that would be medical staff, doctors.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us about the person who is entering the data into the registration book for the persons who are admitted into the hospital, what does that person fill in, in the part of the registration book for the person which is admitted in the hospital? What is entered?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The time of admission, name, surname, date of birth, diagnosis, upon admittance, address.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When is that entered?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When is the diagnosis entered?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Diagnosis, diagnosis is entered following the examination. What I said, the data is entered immediately if this person knows it. If it has an ID or something on the basis of which these data can be entered. The diagnosis is done, was entered following the examination by the doctor, when the doctor ascertains, establishes, what the problem is. So following the examination and upon the order of the doctor, the diagnosis Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. is entered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, may I ask you, the Chamber has now listened for 25 minutes to a lot of details on how these books were established. What is the case of the Defence? Perhaps you could confront the witness with that. Is it a forged book? Is it a book with some imprecisions or are these registers with imprecisions or are these death certificates not perfect or are they all forged? What is the case? Would you please come to your point, because otherwise, I am afraid --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... of everyone. So would you please come to your point.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, when we spoke of the death certificates, you said that the death certificates were signed by the doctor who was the one who ascertained the death of the patient. Could you tell us to whom were these death certificates forwarded?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The death certificates were submitted, one to the family, one to the municipality that is the municipality where the address or the residence of the person killed was and the third copy went to the files, to the archive.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness I am going to ask the usher if you could be given death certificates 3738S, 3738R, and 3738D. Your Honour, for each of the death certificates I would like to have them looked at, but I am going to ask one question, but in order to save time, that is why I wanted several death certificates to be shown to the witness 3738C, 3738B.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, we will first have a look at the death certificate 3738S, is that the first one?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In this certificate it was ascertained that Atif Bajraktarevic died on the 1st of June 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If you can, I would ask you please to turn to the second page of this document. On the first page, is there a seal of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there is no seal. I explained at the time the seal had not been made yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, when was the seal made?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I don't know exactly because the hospital was officially registered at the 10th of May. At that time it was not exactly peace so that we can follow procedures, then following some memoranda and a seal was made, but I don't know exactly when that was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, when I asked you, you said that the death was ascertained by the doctor and that he would then enter the data into the form and he would sign the form?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me on this certificate, 3738S, where is the signature of the doctor?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is none. There is no signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, this copy of this document, is it a true copy of the original, the original that you have at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: But you signed this on the 13th of February -- 13th of January 2002. What did you confirm exactly on this copy, for this document?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this signature of mine was placed here as a confirmation that I had handed over this document. Certainly, I did not sign the death certificate. Here it says 13th of January 2002, which means that when I handed over the documents to the investigators, that is -- sorry -- this is the 13th of January 2002. That is when I was signing that the copies were true copies of the original. And I certainly, I couldn't sign certifying the death.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On the 13th of January 2002, when you placed your signature there by which you certified this was a true copy of the original, on that very moment did you have before you the original of this document?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. How could I have done it otherwise?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, at the time when you signed this document on the 13th of January 2002, did you see before you the original of this document?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably did because I was obviously signing that these were true copies of the original. So I couldn't -- I couldn't just sign like that, a death certificate.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that you did not sign the death certificate, who did sign the death certificate then?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A doctor, the doctor who issued this death certificate.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On this death certificate, could you tell us where the signature of the doctor is?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a fact that I cannot see it here but it probably exists somewhere. It has probably been signed somewhere. Perhaps it is in the archive, in the files.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say there is probably a signature somewhere in the archive --

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sorry. I don't know why this one was submitted and signed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please have a look at the document 3738R?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is there your signature on the first page?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the very same date 13th of January.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is there a seal of the hospital on the first page?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Have a look at page 2 of the document?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where is the signature doctor who issued this death certificate?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no signature on any of these documents, of these four documents. There is no signature of the doctor, I don't know why. My signature is here only in order to certify that I was the one who handed over these documents. These were the documents that I handed over to the investigator. So this is not my signature that is on the death certificate. I did not ascertain the death of the patient.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say of all these four documents --

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of all these documents that you showed me four or five documents let us not waste time, this is the same case for all of them.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And B.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to show the witness certificates 3738K, 3737J, 3738F. Your Honour I notice that in the transcript, it doesn't say 3738F, as I said J and K.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, if we are using these numbers, perhaps we should make better clear to those who transcribe the documents. The first set of documents you showed to the witness was 3738S from Simon, B from Benjamin, C from character, D from Danijel, and R from Richard. I am not certainly not using the proper names for spelling out in English. And you are now showing to the witness 3738K from Kelly, F from fox trot and J from -- I have difficulties in the spelling alphabet in English. I have had not enough training to do my job properly. J would be from JNA.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please look at these three documents. These are the documents, death certificates for the 12th of July 1993. On page 2 of each of the documents, there is a name of the doctor. Could you please tell us who signed these certificates?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see the signature of the doctor on any of these. They have probably been mistakenly copied. They are unsigned. I don't understand how this happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, when you were signing your own name, when you were signing these documents, did you check whether these documents were true copies of the original, about which you say that exist in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I put my signature when I was handing over the documents. All of the documents were brought by the persons who were in charge for the documents. These are the people who worked in the archive, in the files, for the registration books. I was authorised to represent the hospital in the absence of Dr. Hajir for the third parties.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, when you placed the signature on these documents, who is the person who brought these documents to you?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall. Probably the person who was working on the registration book.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Since you were responsible for the archive, for the files --

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Among others.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was it your responsibility, your duty, since you had to put your signature there, was it your responsibility to check whether these were the true copies of the originals which are contained in the archive?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not think about doubting the authenticity because there was no reason for anything to be forged.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you confirming to us now that these documents are copies of the original, as we can look at them now, originals do exist in the archive?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They certainly exist.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you signed these documents, at that time when you signed them, did you notice that there was no signature of the doctor?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was probably an oversight on my part.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, would you allow for the possibility that the documents that you had a look at now and for which that you said that they were unsigned by the doctor who ascertained the death of these persons whose names and surnames we have that these documents were made at a later date?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were certainly not made at a later date, later on. This is just a small section of the documentation which exists in the Dobrinja hospital, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us where is the original archive located of the Dobrinja hospital?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of the documents, all of the files of the documents after the hospital closed is located in the central archive.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am looking at the time. I have for another 10 minutes after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then let me just ask Ms. Mahindaratne, are we moving to the next witness after the break where we might need half an hour preparation?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, I would prefer, as a matter of fact, because otherwise, we would have a break of half an hour now, and then continue for 10 minutes, and then we would need another.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am informed that we need no specific time to prepare for the next witness, as far as the technicians are concerned. So we will have a break now until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Madam, at the Dobrinja hospital, have there been any other cases of death, so to say, which were not a direct consequence of injury of wounds, I mean, regular patients admitted to hospital and dying there?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Presumably. Because that was the hospital that treated the so-called regular or normal patients.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like the witness to be shown the document 37475 or B rather than five. P3747.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said 3747 -- yes. I see.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us when it was issued?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document is not dated. There is no clear date of issue, but obviously it was compiled after the events of the 1st of June 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us when it was drawn up?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Presumably the day after.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When I presented you with a death certificate for June 1993, you mentioned that there was no seal of the hospital because the hospital did not have a seal. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In that case, maybe this document was issued later. I can see that there is a seal on this one. Maybe it was compiled later on, this report, I mean, because there was considerable number of both dead and injured and it took some time to get all the papers sorted out.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Madam, can you tell us when this document was drawn up? When you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. say "later" when later?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who compiled this document?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is obviously something which is printed out of a computer. It must have been compiled by the operator who entered the data originally, and who was therefore in charge of the report which he had then went on to draw up.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you give us the name and the surname of the operator who compiled these reports?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was Mr. Sead Devesovic [phoen] so he would compile these reports on the basis of the existing documents, on the data that he entered into to the computer, and according to the need, he would print out the reports.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say it was then approved by those in charge, can you tell us who approved these documents?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since you can more or less see the seal on this copy, well, I can't really see a signature here. But I believe that he had a part of the responsibility and therefore I believe he could have signed the report himself. But generally speaking, it was not up to him. He did not do it. Either Dr. Hajir -- one of the doctors or occasionally myself. Because there was no reason to doubt the accuracy of the data.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where your signature is on this document?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already said that. You can't see anybody's signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that there is an original in the archives at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose there is. Since this was a significant document for the hospital, there certainly is an original.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you saying that in case we were to be shown the original, that we would see the signatures of the people who approved the document?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Madam, can we agree that the register of the hospital was compiled by hand, the one that you recognised earlier on?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that the data from that register which was compiled by hand were at the same time entered into the computer?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe not throughout the period, because initially we probably did not have a computer.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "initially we did not have a computer," as far as you can tell, for how long did the hospital have a computer and for how long did the operator work on it?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1993, when I arrived, there was a computer and there was a computer operator.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: For how long did he remain on the job?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the hospital closed down.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, is there any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I want to just ask three questions, Mr. President, if I may be permitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Witness, you handed over a number of documents, a large number of documents to the investigators of the Tribunal, when you made your statement in 1995?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: In addition to the ones shown to you today?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: It was not that you selected documents relating to these three dates with regard to which the documents were shown to you but you gave additionally many documents?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: You were shown a couple of -- a few death certificates without the doctor's signature?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can you give a possible explanation as to how doctor's signature can be absent from in those documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object to the question for the simple reason that we should specify "copies" since the witness's statement was that presumably the signatures did exist on the originals of these documents. That is what I understood at least. And as a consequence, if the witness is saying that the signatures were present in the original then asking these questions simply causes confusion. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that the question was, Ms. Mahindaratne, that the witness would have an explanation for the absence of the doctor's signatures on the copies of the death certificates that were shown to her?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, as I understand, the witness did not at any stage say that the signatures would be definitely there in the original documents, in the archives. She could not -- I am merely asking for a plausible explanations as to how the doctor's signature could be absent --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but on the documents as shown to her, that means the documents that came from the archives?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have an explanation why these documents shown to you do not show a signature of the doctor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know, believe me. Because if you go to 50 or 60 patients all at the same time, those were mere formalities, and it was much more important to attend to the patients and try and save their lives and do what we could. I don't really have an explanation, apart from the fact that we had to act swiftly.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I know I have gone beyond three questions, Mr. President. I am just trying to clarify on this. Just give me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: At any stage could you with certainty say that the original documents of those copies which were shown to you without the doctor's signature would have the doctor's signature there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this question too is a leading question because we have not -- I mean, the witness has not been supplied with the originals here, and this is a question based on an assumption basically, because these originals are not likely to be submitted today or can't be submitted today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but the question is not whether they would be submitted today, but whether you can ask questions about originals that still remain -- let me just have a look at the question once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, could you please rephrase the question, because the wording is not clear enough. I mean, the original documents of those copies is -- could be still several documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Witness, you authenticated, you signed the copies which were shown to you after comparing them with the original documents?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the original documents is the documents that are in the archives of the hospital. That is what you call the originals at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please rephrase again.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Witness, you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any other objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there is another one. Since I am not at all certain that the specific statement of the witness was that she actually compared each and every one of these copies with the original. She did not say that she compared each single copy to every single original which presumably exists somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You should keep that in mind as well while rephrasing your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President. Let me ask this question in a different way.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Witness, you have authenticated each and every copy which was shown to you in court today with your signature?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I can state with certainty that none of the documents submitted to the Prosecution and submitted to this Court have been falsified or forged. Because there was simply no reason for that. We could have supplied you ten times as many documents of this sort.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So you have -- you had no doubt whatsoever of its authenticity when you signed the document?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: None, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That is all, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Nieto-Navia has one or more questions to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I would like the document 3738R to be shown to the witness and put on the ELMO, please. Would you please point out to your signature there. No. You have to use the --

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I would like you to have a look on document 3738K. Could you point out to your signature on that document?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: That signature was made -- do you have the date of your signature there?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the signature was placed at the time when the documents were handed in because when I was handing those documents over to the Prosecution, I put my signature on every one. Obviously, I could not have certified the document myself. I am not the person who ascertained death and put my signature there. I hope that that much is clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: So the signature on document 3738R was made at a later date probably?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: No further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge El Mahdi also has a question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. [Interpretation] I would like you to explain to me the procedure which refers to the issuing of the death certificates? If my understanding is correct, you said that each certificate entails one original and two copies. One of which is sent to the municipal authorities and another one is kept on file. Normally, the doctor's signature is placed on both the copies and the originals, or the original only?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally speaking, it should be placed on both, the copies and the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one question related to this one as well. Do you consider it to be possible that those copies that were sent out from the hospital, either given to the family of the deceased patient or to the municipality, would be signed while the copy remaining in the hospital would not be signed? So the archived copy not signed, and the other copies that left the hospital would be signed? Would that be possible in your view?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not certain but I believe that if it is important, probably these certificates, that is to say, the fact that it had been ascertained that somebody did die, could be obtained from our competent authorities, the family or the archives. Is this of consequence for the Court, I believe it is certainly possible to prove that the persons that these death certificates referred to -- I mean, obviously I can guarantee you, you don't have to believe me, you can't believe me but in each individual case proof can be found that these people actually died. I mean nobody could have been that much sick in the head to issue a death certificate for somebody who was not dead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that --

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are more ways of proving --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question was whether you consider it to be Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. possible that it was an unsigned copy that remained in the hospital where the copies that would leave the hospital would be signed?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not certain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I am asking you not for --

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... whether you would consider this to be possible or not.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I have the next question for you: You remember the document with the badly legible parts on the bottom. That is P3747. Could it perhaps be given to the witness again. On this list, do you recognise names of persons that you knew and according to your knowledge were injured or wounded at the 1st of June 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know them personally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but if not personally, in what way would you know any of them? Take your time to go through the list. It is a long list.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I am leafing through this, I have just remembered that one of the best friends of my son actually was killed. He was 19 years old at the end so I am looking for his name. I remember that it was on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you give his family name, we could perhaps even assist you.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] I know his name. [Interpretation] His name was Fejzo. I can't remember his family name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you can't find it, it is no problem. So you do not recognise any person known personally by you who appears on this list?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This Mitro Malicbegovic was a colleague of my brother who also worked at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where do we find him?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is page eight. Line 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the name so that --

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mitro Malicbegovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And do you have any personal knowledge that he was wounded or killed?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, he was injured.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He was injured. Yes. Thank you. Then I have a last question for you: When you handed over these documents in 1995, could I please ask you in more detail on how this happened? You were asked to provide documents. Did you ask those who are in charge of the archives to give them to you or were they brought to you without giving any instruction to those to do so? So who asked you to produce them and to whom did you ask to give them to you?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The hospital on that day was visited by investigators from the The Hague. There was an interpreter with them. And there were two or three of them in any case, and they wanted to see the documents. I don't know for which period, but in any case, what they asked for, what we were able to give them at the time, I had -- I was also requested from the people who were working on the records, and they brought the documentation in order to compare them to the certificates so that the registration book would be compared and copied. Anything that they needed, any certificates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to do it a bit more in detail. Did the investigators first come to you? Did they come to your office?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Investigators came to the office of Dr. Hajir. I think that on that day he had some duties, so he was not there. I believe that they were there for two days. I am not quite sure. That was some time ago. And he had authorised me, he said that to the investigators would come, that I should receive them, that I should hand over to them whatever they ask for the documentation. So I should be at their disposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So they came to Dr. Hajir, and then he said that they would have to meet with you. Did they then indicate to you what they wanted to see or what they wanted to have? I mean, documents --

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably documentation. About -- I don't know -- about the injured, about the killed, probably.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What did you do then? Did you go with them to the archives or did you ask someone in charge of the archives to bring it to you? How did it exactly happen? Did you go to the archive or did you ask the person of the archive to come to you?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally did not take and copy the documents, but I asked the person in charge of the archive to bring the documents, I presume, for a certain period, because obviously they couldn't fetch all of the documentation because it is an enormous amounts of documents. And for these documents to be copied and to be brought.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
