utterances.text: Yes. So you asked personally the responsible person for the archives to get the documents from the archives and to have them copied for you?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At that very moment, how much time did that take, approximately? You asked for it were they brought that same day, that same morning or afternoon or did it take a couple of days?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in succession.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As they copied the documents, they then brought it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that was during that same meeting that they brought the or the next day or one week afterwards or?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It took approximately -- I don't know. I think it may have been two days. I am not quite sure. I think it lasted -- well, it lasted because there were a lot of documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then they brought them to you?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's right. I think that I was in the same office as the investigators, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They then brought the documents, they entered it into the computers. I don't know what they did. They had their own laptop computers, and that is what they did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the documents were brought to you in another meeting with the investigators and then you handed them over and you did not exactly know what they did with it? I mean, how they worked on it or? But it was after two days, approximately, that the documents were produced by the archives --

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And was it in a meeting with the investigators that you handed them over to them?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was at that time they also took the statement from me, as it were, that I was handing over these documents that I am letting them have a look at the documents, that I was stating and confirming that these were the authentic documents. And they also asked me if there was need for any additional information, additional statements, whether I would be able to confirm this, and I, of course, said that I would be able to, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So am I right in understanding that the documents came from the archives to you and then that you handed them over to the Prosecutor -- to the investigators and that they were not directly given by the persons of the archive to the investigators, but it was through you?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were in the same office, the investigators and myself, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is clear to me. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may point out, the name of Mitro Malicbegovic has gone down on the record incorrectly. The name the witness gave as somebody whom she knew in the list P3747.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: In the record the name has not been --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are talking about Malicbegovic is that correct? As the person you knew and that was injured on that day.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a brother of a friend of mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But the name was Malicbegovic.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last name, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is m-a-l-i-c-b-e-g-o-v-i-c. The name -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour the Defence has one question in relation to Mitro Malicbegovic if the witness could have a look at the document. Bearing in mind she said that it was on the 1st of June 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes could P3747 -- is that still in front of you, yes. Would you look at the page where you find Mr. Malicbegovic --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you find it, Witness.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us the date which is next to this witness?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 28th of July 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: I have a question, but it is a question for Ms. Mahindaratne. On the same document, please, go to the second page to the page which has some handwritten words in B/C/S and a date.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Could you please indicate where is the translation of that page?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour translations have been provided -- if I may just have a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Yes. Translation is Exhibit 37 -- 3747.1

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, just pointed out the handwritten portion as to why that portion has not been translated, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: The page.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I have the translation page, Your Honour, but I do agree that that portion has not been translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Which is the page of the translation?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: If I may just have a moment, Your Honour. That portion is translated, Your Honour. I beg Your Honour's pardon. The page is -- I could give the ERN number 03055588. It is out of sequence, I am told, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: I don't have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the last two digits, because I also cannot find it. On the transcript it reads "88."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: I don't have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, as far as the translation is concerned, I find different numbers on it. On the top of the translation it starts at 0026, but then it is 52, last two digits, and it goes until 59, last two digits. And then we have other numbers, stamped numbers, which start with 47 and then go to 60. So no 88.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may have some time, I will be able to provide photocopies. I am told, that in fact in providing the copies to Court and Defence the pages have been mixed up. So as per the copies I have here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I perhaps first see your page 88 so that we can see whether we have similar documents as you have.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The copies you are working from are certainly not the same as we are working from. The whole format is totally different. So -- yes, well that of course creates quite some confusion. I see that on your document there seems to be a text translated similar to what we could think of, but could you clarify the issue during the next break.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Because I realise that the documents that you have at the moment is what was tendered with the 92 bis package.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, I am presented with P3747 and a translation. If you say the order is not correct I could only confirm that because it is not the same order of names and, well to say at least, this takes a lot of time and creates confusion and nothing else at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, Mr. President. May I just point out after the break --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you may. Ms. Arifagic, unfortunately, we had to deal with this procedural aspect while you were still waiting. You have answered all the questions of the Bench and of both the parties. I would like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and to testify in this court. And you are now excused. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. May I ask you, Mr. Usher, to escort Ms. Arifagic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Given the problems that have arisen, the Chamber prefers to deal with the documents after the break. Is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, we are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we first have to turn into --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- private session. But before doing so, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Here we have a serious problems, because all of these documents, there are many of them, there is a voluminous documentation, and we don't really want to though ourselves onto the next witness and then catch up with the documents later on. I think we should be doing it now. These problems should be dealt with now. I think the Prosecution should deal with the problems now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Prosecution asked to clarify the issue of the translation of one of these documents during the break. We allowed them to do so. So it is of no use to deal with the documents at this moment. We will do that after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will then now turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session again. Madam Registrar, I would like to deal now with the documents in respect of the previous witness. The witness, Arifagic, if you would please call the documents and we will then hear what objections there are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I suggest now to do it differently upon the suggestion of the Registrar. First, all the documents will be called and explained what it is and whether it has a translation or not and afterwards I will give an opportunity to the parties to object. And may I then ask the parties to clearly indicate what document we are talking about, what exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it is a point of methodology. One part of the objection is that we might have may be based on matters having to do with the fact that the photocopies are not legible. Shouldn't we do the opposite, provide the best possible copies if we have them, which would cut down on the number of objections. Yes it was my understanding --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... better translations or better copies, whatever, has to be provided. So I do agree with you that we first should give Ms. Mahindaratne the opportunity to submit whatever she additionally wants to submit to the court.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: First of all, Mr. President, I do beg Your Honours' pardon for my inability to be here at the end of the first break to respond to the issue that comes up. And I do beg Your Honours' pardon for the confusion this has created. There is a really plausible explanation. The documents I -- the Prosecution was working on is not a separate set or not an alien set of documents. In fact, the set of documents that the Prosecution has been working on and which was submitted for Your Honours' examination were submitted with the 92 bis package and contains in fact the Registry stamp, that is -- I am referring to P37471 which was tendered with the 92 bis package originally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes but the 92 bis package, we have a decision on 92 bis. So that is not in play any more, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But perhaps the Chamber is more interested in how you would solve the problem than to explain how it could exist. If we have much time available, we could spend hours on trying to explain how this all happened. We are not happy with it. It is confusing, but let's see how we can solve the problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I will briefly explain what happened, Mr. President. In tendering the same document in exhibit form, quite erroneously, we have printed out a separate -- there are old translations in regard to the same document in different format. The substance is the same but when different translators worked on the same document, different formats have been used and therefore documents which were tendered by the Exhibit P37471, yesterday was different to what was submitted with the 92 bis package. And the Prosecution has right along been working on the same set which was what was originally submitted to court the 92 bis package and this was the discrepancy. There is no disparity or any difference between the two documents. The substance is the same, but the form is different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, we established that the lines Judge Nieto-Navia asked for were not in the other translation. So I would say, don't explain that it is all the same, one out of 10 translations Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. because it was not the same translation of the original document. So, as I asked you before, please solve the problem, instead of explaining us of giving us an explanation which is at the same time not very satisfactory and at least as far as the identity of the translations are concerned, is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President. May I be permitted to tender P37471 which is the document we have been using which can be distributed now -- has been distributed

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it has been distributed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And there, if Your Honours be pleased to examine page three --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have got to 37471 and I have got two documents, but they don't carry the same name. Is it 37471A or what? I don't have the same titles here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I noticed that in the earlier translation, but it might be a matter of order, because we were explained as well, that the following order of the pages was not correct. We are not going to compare a document that is not tendered any more with a document that is now being tendered. We are now talking about 3747.1, as presented last by the -- by the Prosecution. And I take it that the loose-leaf ending in 600 should be in place between the stapled 599 and 601. I will find a machine to unstaple it and staple again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would have preferred to have the set all stapled or not stapled at all but not one page loose which should be -- okay, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So the page which was -- which corresponds to page two of the document is in the translation on page three. That is because in translating, because of the language difference, sometimes the names flow on to the next page and therefore you will not find page two of the original corresponding with page two of the translation. So as Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand that if you take landscape instead of portrait, that you can have less names on the page. We will check of course. I take it now that this is a translation of all the text of 3747, although the page numbering might be a bit different. And I also take it that it replaces the document 3747.1 that was distributed before.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.text: Then could we please ask for your assistance, Madam Registrar.
